title: Apply an active skill when a request matches (runtime consumer)
goal: A promoted skill changes how NERV answers a matching request; a staged or retired one never does
acceptance: Owner decision 2026-11-26 in chat: "y" to the skills panel and pre-flight skill plan (earlier: "pre flight check, ok", real data).

Found on 2026-11-26 while planning: nothing in NERV applies a skill at run time today (src/skills.ts is only read by the nerv skills commands; pilots carry skill ids but no code reads the instructions). A failing test (committed first) shows an active skill's instructions reaching the planner prompt for a matching request and nothing for a staged, retired or rolled-back one

Matching is by the skill manifest's domain and an owner-readable trigger list in the manifest, not by a model guess; a skill may use only the read tools its requiredCapabilities names and the tools the owner has granted (checkSkillPermissionEscalation holds at run time too); a skill with a write or approval capability is refused here (read-only skills only in this step)

The instructions enter the prompt as data from the owner-approved package, never from a retrieved page; the tool calls the skill leads to still pass the gate at the executor; the sorties and the replies name the skill and its version
privacy: Neutral invented skills, fleets, spots and weather only; no owner data, tokens or coordinates of a real place in Git or tests.
escalation: A material scope or effort increase goes to the owner
A skill that could write or approve anything is out of scope and goes to the owner as a separate decision

effort.basis: Estimated 2026-11-26: a small matcher and one prompt insertion point in the planner, plus tests that staged and retired skills never apply; the insertion point carries the uncertainty. Not a measurement.
